source_text:
Epilogus alius. Ταῦτα μετεγράψατο μὲν Γάϊος ἐκ τῶν Εἰρηναίου συγγραμμάτων, ὃς καὶ συνεπολιτεύσατο τῷ Εἰρηναίῳ, μαθητῇ γεγονότι τοῦ ἁγίου Πολυκάρπου. Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Εἰρηναῖος, κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ μαρτυρίου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου Πολυκάρπου γενόμενος ἐν Ῥώμῃ, πολλοὺς ἐδίδαξεν· οὗ καὶ πολλὰ συγγράμματα κάλλιστα καὶ ὀρθότατα φέρεται, ἐν οἷς μέμνηται Πολυκάρπου, ὅτι παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἔμαθεν· ἱκανῶς τε πᾶσαν αἵρεσιν ἤλεγξεν καὶ τὸν ἐκκλησιαστικὸν κανόνα καὶ καθολικόν, ὡς παρέλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ παρέδωκεν. Λέγει δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ὅτε συναντήσαντός ποτε τῷ ἁγίῳ Πολυκάρπῳ Μαρκίωνος, ἀφ᾽ οὗ οἱ λεγόμενοι Μαρκιωνισταί, καὶ εἰπόντος· Ἐπιγίνωσκέ ἡμᾶς, Πολύκαρπε, εἶπεν αὐτὸς τῷ Μαρκίωνι· Ἐπιγινώσκω, ἐπιγινώσκω τὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ σατανᾶ. Καὶ τοῦτο δὲ φέρεται ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Εἰρηναίου συγγράμμασιν, ὅτι τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ὥρᾳ ἐν Σμύρνῃ ἐμαρτύρησεν ὁ Πολύκαρπος, ἤκουσεν φωνὴν ἐν τῇ Ῥωμαίων πόλει ὑπάρχων ὁ Εἰρηναῖος ὡς σάλπιγγος λεγούσης· Πολύκαρπος ἐμαρτύρησεν.

Ἐκ τούτου οὖν, ὡς προλέλεκται, τῶν τοῦ Εἰρηναίου συγγραμμάτων Γάϊος μετεγράψατο, ἐκ δὲ τῶν Γαΐου ἀντιγράφων Ἰσοκράτης ἐν Κορίνθῳ. Ἐγὼ δὲ πάλιν Πιόνιος ἐκ τῶν Ἰσοκράτους ἀντιγράφων ἔγραψα, κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν τοῦ ἁγίου Πολυκάρπου ζητήσας αὐτά, συναγαγὼν αὐτὰ ἤδη σχεδὸν ἐκ τοῦ χρόνου κεκμηκότα, ἵνα κἀμὲ συναγάγῃ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς μετὰ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἐπουράνιον αὐτοῦ βασιλείαν· ᾧ ἡ δόξα σὺν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
thought_title: Chain of copying and two memories from Irenaeus
orientation: A later copyist note traces how this letter passed from Irenaeus through Gaius and Isocrates to Pionius after the martyrdom account has ended.
pass_a_gloss: Another epilogue. These things Gaius transcribed from the writings of Irenaeus, who also shared a common citizenship with Irenaeus, who had become a disciple of holy Polycarp. For this Irenaeus, when he was in Rome at the time of the martyrdom of Polycarp the bishop, taught many; and many writings of his, most excellent and most correct, are in circulation, in which he remembers Polycarp, that he learned from him; and he sufficiently exposed every heresy and handed on the church rule and universal one, as he received it from the holy one, and he handed it on. And he says also this, that when Marcion, from whom come those called Marcionites, once met with holy Polycarp and said, Recognize us, Polycarp, he himself said to Marcion, I recognize, I recognize the first born of Satan. And this also is reported in the writings of Irenaeus, that on the day and hour in which Polycarp suffered martyrdom in Smyrna, Irenaeus, while being in the city of the Romans, heard a voice as of a trumpet saying, Polycarp suffered martyrdom. From this then, as has been said before, from the writings of Irenaeus Gaius transcribed, and from the copies of Gaius Isocrates in Corinth. And I again, Pionius, wrote from the copies of Isocrates, after I sought them out by revelation of holy Polycarp, after I gathered them when they were already almost worn out by time, in order that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me with his elect into his heavenly kingdom; to whom be the glory with the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit unto the ages of the ages, amen.

lemmas.gloss: shared citizenship with, lived as fellow citizen

choices.why: brief glossary requires martyrdom for μαρτύριον
brief glossary requires universal for καθολικός, not confessional Catholic
keeps intransitive force that Polycarp underwent death rather than caused it

choices.term: Ἐπιγινώσκω, ἐπιγινώσκω τὸν πρωτότοκον τοῦ σατανᾶ
choices.english: I recognize, I recognize the first born of Satan
choices.why: keeps doubled present verb and plain genitive without hyphenated compound

pass_b_english: Gaius transcribed this account from the writings of Irenaeus, who was also his fellow citizen. Irenaeus had been a disciple of holy Polycarp. He was in Rome at the time of the martyrdom of Polycarp the bishop, and there he taught many people. Many writings of his are preserved, finest and truest in their kind. In them he mentions Polycarp and says that he learned from him. He ably refuted every heresy, and he handed on the ecclesiastical and universal rule of the church just as he had received it from the holy one.

He tells this story too. Marcion once met holy Polycarp, the Marcionists being those called after Marcion, and Marcion said, "Recognize us, Polycarp." Polycarp said to Marcion, "I recognize, I recognize the first born of Satan." His writings also preserve this report. On the day and at the hour when Polycarp suffered martyrdom in Smyrna, Irenaeus was in the city of Rome and heard a voice like a trumpet saying, "Polycarp suffered martyrdom."

As has been said before, then, Gaius transcribed his text from the writings of Irenaeus, and Isocrates in Corinth worked from the copies of Gaius. And I, Pionius, have written it out again from the copies of Isocrates. I sought out these writings in obedience to a revelation of holy Polycarp, and I gathered them when they were already almost worn out by time, so that the Lord Jesus Christ may also gather me with his elect into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory with the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit to the ages of ages, amen.
notes: Latin heading Epilogus alius is preserved as given, not translated as part of Greek.
Copyist name here is Ἰσοκράτης, differing by one letter from Socrates in the preceding ending; gloss keeps what is here.
Phrase τὸν ἐκκλησιαστικὸν κανόνα καὶ καθολικόν leaves καθολικόν without an explicit noun; gloss keeps adjectives substantive.
